I am 42 years old, and I have been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for five years now. Before that I worked in Shijiazhuang after university, so I did not grow up in the fields like my father did. But those five years have taught me that book knowledge only gets you halfway — the other half comes from watching your own plots and listening to the neighbors who have been here for decades.

My wife works part-time at a garment factory in town, and my parents help with the children, so between the four of us the labor available for the farm is tight. I cannot afford to waste days on unnecessary tillage or too many hand-sprayed pesticide rounds. I rely on the tube well for irrigation, which is reliable but the electricity bill adds up, so I count every irrigation.

I put all 6 mu into the wheat–maize rotation. That is the system everyone around me uses, and after five years I know my soil can handle it. For wheat, I sow in mid-October with an improved variety — I have been using Luyuan 502 for three years and it has done well on my land. I rotary-till before sowing to break up the wheat stubble from the previous maize cycle and get a fine seedbed. For fertilizer, I base my rates on what I learned in school and what the county extension office recommends, but I also watch the color of my neighbor's wheat when I walk past his field every morning. I put down about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing — the 15-15-15 type — which gives me roughly 7–8 kg of N, P, and K each. Then at green-up in spring I topdress with another 15 kg per mu of urea, and if the plants look pale at jointing I add one more 10 kg splash. That brings my total nitrogen to about 22 kg per mu, phosphorus around 6 kg, and potassium around 4 kg. I irrigate four times: the critical winter irrigation before freeze-up to protect the roots, one at green-up, one at jointing, and one during grain filling. For pesticides, I spray three times — herbicide at tillering, insecticide for aphids before flag leaf, and a fungicide if I see any rust spots.

After wheat harvest in early June, the turnaround to maize is brutally short — sometimes less than a week. I do not till for maize; I plant directly into the wheat stubble with a no-till planter I hire from the village cooperative. Time is money in that window. I buy fresh hybrid seed every year, Denghai 605 usually, because saved seed loses vigor and the hybrid advantage is real. I band about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting, then side-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. Total N comes to about 18 kg per mu, P around 5 kg, K around 3 kg. I irrigate twice — once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once at the big-flare tasseling stage. Three pesticide applications: a pre-emergence herbicide, one spray for armyworm when the ears are forming, and one more if the neighbor's field starts showing mold.

I am targeting about 520 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize. Last year I got 500 and 530, and the soil is in good shape, so I think 520 and 550 are realistic if we do not get a freak drought. I would rather apply a little too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and with only 6 mu I cannot afford a big yield drop.
